title: Naqareh (copper kettle drums)
summary: The naqareh is a pair of small kettle drums with copper bowls and skin heads laced with leather. The larger drum gives a deep note and the smaller a higher one. Played with two light sticks, the pair has long been a signal and dance drum across Iran and the Caucasus.
howToPlay: Two kettle drums stand in carved cradles: the large one on the left, the small one on the right. Each has a centre and a crescent along its near rim to strike.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
The centre gives a round note, the edge a quick, sharp one.
Learn the gallop first, then the fanfare.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The gallop counts six beats to the bar; the fanfare counts four.
heritageNote: Pairs of kettle drums like the naqareh were played on horseback and at gatherings, to give signals and to set the pace of dances. The copper bowl and the laced skin give a bright, ringing note.
